key_insight: Neuroevolution, especially evolution strategies, provides a stronger stability-plasticity balance than standard continual RL methods in changing tasks by optimizing directly in weight space.
engineering_relevance: For continual control and adaptive engineering systems, neuroevolution can be a practical alternative when models must keep learning without catastrophic forgetting.
method: Compared evolution strategies (ES) and genetic algorithms (GA) against continual RL and population-based RL baselines.
Analyzed return landscapes around learned solutions to assess robustness and task-to-task overlap in weight space.
Tested both small and large policies across a wide range of environments and environmental changes.
evidence_signal: Across many environments and network sizes, ES most consistently balanced adaptation and forgetting, while GA adapted faster but forgot more; neighborhood overlap in weight space correlated with this trade-off.
watch_item: Results come from benchmark environments and weight-space perturbation analysis, so transfer to safety-critical deployed systems may require additional validation and tuning.
